rot.distant.ideia.ex1.e1: You already know the key squares and direct opposition. Now the kings start further apart.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.e5: For this pawn, the key squares are f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.e6: The fight begins: your king wants a key square; the black king wants g6, in front of the pawn, guarding all three.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! Your king advances toward the key squares.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to advance the king to e4, toward the key squares.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3d4.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3d4.2: The black king goes to f7, on its way to g6: from there, in front of the pawn, it controls f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c4.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c4.2: The black king goes to f7, on its way to g6: from there, in front of the pawn, it controls f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3e3.1: It looks natural, but with that move White no longer wins.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3e3.2: The black king goes to e7 and faces it, three squares away. Now the opposition belongs to Black.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c3.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c3.2: The black king goes to f7, on its way to g6: from there, in front of the pawn, it controls f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3e2.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3e2.2: The black king goes to f7, on its way to g6: from there, in front of the pawn, it controls f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3d2.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3d2.2: The black king goes to f7, on its way to g6: from there, in front of the pawn, it controls f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c2.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.d3c2.2: The black king goes to f7, on its way to g6: from there, in front of the pawn, it controls f5, g5 and h5.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.g3g4.1: Pushing the pawn now does not win: Black can draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.err.g3g4.2: The black king runs to f7 and will arrive in time in front of the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing with White and see how Black defends.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: The black king always closes the way.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.fins.limite: The black king always closes the way.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l1: Notice: your king went to e4, the black king's file. Now there are three empty squares between the kings.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l2: You already know direct opposition: kings face to face, one square between them, held by the side that has just moved.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l4: With three squares between the kings, it is the distant opposition: as they close in, it turns into direct opposition.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l5: To know who has it, count the empty squares between the kings on the same file or rank.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l6: An odd number after your move: the opposition is yours. Here, the king on e4 left three squares: White has it.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l7: If it were even, the other king would step up and leave the odd number. So, with each move, leave an odd number.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l8: Black has several defences. Let's start with the one that gives White the most trouble.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l9: Black brings the king to f7, heading toward the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l10: Their plan is to reach g6 and get in front of the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l11: You get there first: with the king on f5, you face the black king.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l12: This is the direct opposition. And f5 is a key square: the black king can no longer reach g6.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l13: Why not push the pawn, which looks so natural? The black king would reach g6, in front of it, and shut you out. Watch.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l14: Go back one move. Imagine that, instead of taking the king to f5, White pushes the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l15: Black answers with the king on g6, right in front of the pawn. It is the ideal spot for the defense.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l16: The white king goes to f4, next to the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l17: The black king faces it. Now the opposition belongs to Black, and the white king cannot pass.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l22: The pawn advanced too early, and the opposition went to Black: it is a draw. That is why the king goes first. Back to the main line.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l23: With the king on g7, Black tries again to get in front of the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l24: You follow with the king to g5 and face it again.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l25: Another key square taken. Now the pawn advances, protected by the king, and promotes.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l26: Now let's go back to the position after the first move.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l27: To recap: your king is on e4, with the distant opposition.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l28: What if Black defends another way, with the king on e7?
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l29: You go to e5 and follow the black king, always face to face, to g5, a key square. You know the rest.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l34: Back to the starting position. Against other defences the plan holds: win the opposition and reach a key square.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l35: Keep the idea: the king goes in front of the pawn and wins the opposition. The pawn only advances afterwards.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l36: Now let's look at the defence: how Black uses the opposition to shut the way.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.e1: Now you play Black, and the board turns around. White has just moved the king to e3.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.e2: With the right defence, Black holds this position.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.e4: The white king wants to reach f5, g5 or h5, the pawn's key squares.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.e5: Your king must shut that path, and the means is the one from the attack: winning the distant opposition.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! Now the distant opposition is yours.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to bring the king to e7: the distant opposition now belongs to Black.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.alt.e8f7.1: Exactly! With the king on f7, Black holds the draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8f8.1: This move loses: now White can win.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8f8.2: On f4, the white king is on your king's file, three squares apart, with Black to move: the distant opposition is his.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8d8.1: This move loses: now White can win.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8d8.2: The white king goes to f4, next to f5 and g5: from d8, your king cannot get there in time to control them.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8d7.1: This move loses: now White can win.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.err.e8d7.2: The white king goes to f4, next to f5 and g5: from d7, your king cannot get there in time to control them.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing with Black and see how White attacks.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.coroa: The pawn promoted. Without the opposition, Black cannot hold.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.limite: The white king controls the key squares: the pawn will promote.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.repeticao: The white king controls the key squares: the pawn will promote.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.capturado: The pawn fell: your king won the fight for the key squares, and it is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: The black king was stalemated: stalemate is a draw, and the defence held.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l1: Three squares between the kings, odd, and you have just moved: the opposition is yours; White must give way.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l2: White has several tries. Let's start with the most direct one.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l3: White advances the king through the center.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l4: You answer by facing it, on e6: direct opposition.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l5: The white king goes to f4, next to the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l6: Your king follows to f6 and faces it again: direct opposition.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l7: With no way through for the white king, White pushes the pawn.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l8: Your king goes to g6, in front of the pawn: the ideal spot for the defense.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l9: The white king reaches no key square. It is a draw.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l10: Now let's go back to the position with your king on e7.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l11: What if, instead of seeking the opposition, the white king goes straight to f4?
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l12: You face it again, on f6. The opposition is still yours.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l13: And what if, instead of stepping up to f6, your king goes to f7, near g8, the promotion square, to defend from behind?
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l14: That gives up the opposition: the white king, already on f4, reaches f5, a key square, first, and the pawn promotes.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l15: White takes advantage: the king goes to f5, takes a key square and faces the black king. The pawn will promote.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l16: That is why, against the king on f4, the answer is f6: facing it, keeping the opposition.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l17: Back to the position with your king on e7. In defence, whoever holds the opposition shuts off the key squares.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.l18: Win the opposition and bring the king in front of the pawn.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.1: First position: the pawn is one rank further back, on the second rank.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.2: The key squares move back with the pawn: now they are f4, g4 and h4.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.3: Your king steps up to e3, on the same file as the black king.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.4: Count the squares between the kings: three, an odd number, and you have just moved. The distant opposition is yours.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.5: Black heads for the pawn with the king on f7.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.6: Your king reaches f4, which is already a key square.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.7: Black goes to g6 and stands in front of the pawn.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.8: You stand face to face on g4: direct opposition, on a key square.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.9: That is the winning move: you keep the opposition, and the black king has to step aside.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.10: The black king runs to the corner, and your king stays ahead of the pawn all the way to g6.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.16: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.17: What if White pushes the pawn at once, two squares, to g4?
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.18: With the pawn on g4, the key squares move up with it, to f6, g6 and h6, and the black king is one step from f6.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.19: Black brings the king to f6 and guards the key squares.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.20: The white king comes to help, but it is far from the key squares f6, g6 and h6.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.21: The black king attacks the pawn and stands in front of it.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.22: White can only defend the pawn. The black king never leaves its path: it is a draw.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.23: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.24: With the pawn further back, the key squares move back too. The king leads with the opposition; the pawn follows.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.1: Second position: the same as before, now from Black's side, and the board has turned.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.2: Only the move has changed. If Black has the move in this position, Black can organize a draw.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.29: When having the move decides who gets the opposition, we say that side has the tempo.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.24: How? By advancing the king to take the opposition before the white king, then standing before the pawn.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.3: Your king steps forward to e6, toward the pawn's key squares.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.4: From here your king can always answer with the opposition. Going to f6 also holds: it also nears the key squares.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.5: White uses the attacking plan: the king goes to e3.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.25: Count: two squares between the kings, even. Step forward and leave one: odd, and the opposition is yours.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.6: You face it on e5. One square between the kings, an odd number, and you have just moved: the opposition is yours.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.7: From here it is the defence of the second example: wherever the white king goes, yours stays facing it.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.15: With the opposition, your king guards the key squares and the white king cannot get through: it is a draw.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.26: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.27: What if Black moves the king to d6, on the white king's file?
rot.distant.demos.tempo.28: Three squares between the kings, and Black has just moved: the distant opposition is theirs. It also holds.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.30: Notice: the black king went to the white king's file, as your king did in the attacking example, going to e4.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.31: Kings on different files? Bring yours to the other's file and leave an odd number of squares: the opposition is yours.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.16: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.17: What if Black moves the king to f7, heading toward the pawn?
rot.distant.demos.tempo.18: Here going to f7 loses: with the pawn on g2, f4 is already a key square, and the white king gets there in two moves.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.19: White takes advantage: the king goes to e3.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.20: Black hurries to g6, in front of the pawn.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.21: Too late: the white king reaches f4, a key square, and the pawn will promote.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.22: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.distant.demos.tempo.23: Same position, opposite results: whoever moves first leaves the odd number, keeps the opposition and decides the ending.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.1: Third position, from Black's side: White moved the king to e2, not to e3.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.2: It looks almost the same, but count the squares between the kings: now there are four.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.3: An even number: White has miscounted. Step forward and leave an odd number: the opposition is yours.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.4: Your king advances to e6. Now there are three squares between the kings, an odd number, and you have just moved.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.5: The distant opposition is yours. Stepping to f6 also holds; any other move hands it back to White.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.7: You stand face to face on e5. It is the same position we saw a moment ago, and it is a draw.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.14: Count the squares between the kings. If your opponent left an even number, step up and take the opposition.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play White and find the best move.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.fim: Your king led the way with the distant opposition, and the pawn advanced only afterwards.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3e3.1: Going to e3, your king reaches the black king's file but leaves four squares between them: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3e3.2: Even: the opposition is Black's. The black king goes to d7 and, if yours goes to d4, goes to d6, facing it, guarding c5.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.1: Going to f4, your king advances off the black king's file and does not win the distant opposition: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.2: The black king goes to d7 and then c6: it gets next to b5 and c5 before yours.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g4.1: Going to g4, your king moves away from the pawn and the key squares a5, b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g4.2: The black king goes to d7 and then c6: it gets next to b5 and c5 before yours.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g3.1: Going to g3, your king moves away from the pawn and the key squares a5, b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g3.2: The black king goes to d7 and then c6: it gets next to b5 and c5 before yours.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g2.1: Going to g2, your king retreats and moves away from the pawn and the key squares a5, b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3g2.2: The black king goes to d7 and then c6: it gets next to b5 and c5 before yours.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3f2.1: Going to f2, your king retreats and loses time in the race to the key squares a5, b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3f2.2: The black king goes to d7 and then c6: it gets next to b5 and c5 before yours.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3e2.1: Going to e2, your king keeps the distant opposition but retreats too far and is late for b5 and c5: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.f3e2.2: The black king goes to d7. Against yours on d3, it holds on c7; on c6, it would lose to yours on c4, facing it.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.b3b4.1: With the pawn on b4 before the king, the key squares move up to a6, b6 and c6: the win slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.ataque.err.b3b4.2: The black king goes to d7, already next to c6; your king, on f3, is far from the new key squares.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play Black and find the best move.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king took the distant opposition in time and did not let the white king through.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7c7.1: Going to c7, your king reaches the white king's file but leaves four squares between them: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7c7.2: Even: the opposition is White's. The kings go up, and White's reaches e4 facing yours on e6.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7b6.1: Going to b6, your king leaves the white king's file and does not win the distant opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7b6.2: The white king goes to d3 and then e4, next to f4, a key square; yours, on b5, is far from the pawn.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7b8.1: Going to b8, your king retreats far from the pawn and does not win the distant opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7b8.2: The white king goes to d3 and then e4, next to f4, a key square, with no fight for the opposition.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7c8.1: Going to c8, your king has the distant opposition but retreats too far and is late for the pawn: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7c8.2: The white king goes up via d2 and e3 and reaches e4 first, facing yours on e6: the direct opposition is White's.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7a8.1: Going to a8, your king moves too far from the pawn: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7a8.2: The pawn advances two squares and runs alone to g8: your king, on a8, cannot catch it.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7a7.1: Going to a7, your king moves too far from the pawn: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7a7.2: The pawn advances two squares and runs alone to g8: your king, on a7, cannot catch it.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7a6.1: Going to a6, your king moves too far from the pawn: the draw slips away.
rot.distant.pratica.defesa.err.b7a6.2: The pawn advances two squares and runs alone to g8: your king, on a6, cannot catch it.
rot.distant.ideia.ex1.l6b: Why? If the black king steps forward, two squares remain; yours steps too, one remains, and he must give way.
rot.distant.ideia.ex2.ponte: I play both sides in three positions now. See who wins the opposition and if the attacker gets a key square.
rot.distant.demos.fileiraAbaixo.10b: Only now does the pawn advance, protected by the king, and promote.
rot.distant.demos.erroAtacante.ponte: Your turn: one attack and one defence against the machine. Before each move, count the squares between the kings.
